The rest of the note is names, location, villages, clan exogamy, migration history, multilingualism (Hausa widespread, some English) and endangerment; no phoneme inventory, no tone marks except on the names ɛBoze/iPanawa.
new_statements.rule_in_words: First-hand survey remark (Blench's own Dec 2003 wordlist elicitation) that iPanawa has a tone system and that it differs markedly from that of its closest relative ɛBoze (which Blench 2018/2020 describe with three-to-four level tones plus contour tones); no tone inventory, no tone rules and no mention of stress or accent for Panawa.
new_statements.identity_note: EDITION OF AN ON-FILE WORK, added: an open, citable published locus (FEL Ogmios newsletter #23, ogmios.org PDF with text) for the Blench & Nengel 2004 note that our bibliography holds only as the Internet Archive copy of the unpublished ms ('read: silent on stress'). Text of the Panawa note is the same as the ms (names unuPanawa/anaPanawa/iPanawa, five villages of Toro LGA, Bauchi State, history, closest language ɛBoze). Explicitly iPanawa = Bujiyel [pwb], Jere cluster, Northern Jos group of East Kainji -- this languoid.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid record pana1298 and reference records 586185 (Blench 2021) and 18723 (Blench & Nengel 2004).
sources.note: Glottolog's fullest description is only a wordlist; no grammar, sketch or phonology reference exists for the language.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2020. The East Kainji languages of Central Nigeria. Afrika und Übersee 93: 45-67. doi:10.15460/auue.2020.93.1.210 (and the 2004 ms. version 'The status of the East Kainji languages of Central Nigeria: recent research').
sources.note: Phonology section (3.1) treats Boze only (consonants, vowels, four level tones + glides); Panawa appears only in the list of languages surveyed since 2003 and in the 'arm, hand' comparative table (iPanawa ù-wáré / tì-wáré). The word 'stress' does not occur.

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. East Kainji opening page of rogerblench.info, Internet Archive copy 2015-04-20 through 2025-05-28 (live domain now squatted by an unrelated site).
sources.note: Directory listing only: the sole Panawa item ever posted is 'Notes on the '; no wordlist, phonology or grammar file for Panawa in any capture.

sources.note: Nothing. Sec. 2.2 Panawa [=Bujiyel] (pp. 6-7) repeats the 2004 note ('the tone system is markedly different') and adds: 'No linguistic work has been undertaken on iPanawa, and there is no informal development.'

sources.note: Nothing; names, location, population (3500, Blench 2003, five villages), source Blench & Nengel (2003); no linguistic references listed.

sources.note: iPanawa occurs only inside the Jere-cluster classification string (ɛBoze-iGusu-iZele-iBunu-iPanawa-iLoro); nothing on its phonology.

sources.note: The only linguistic data ever collected on Panawa; a tone-marked wordlist with Blench's usual phonology preamble would be the sole possible locus of any remark on tone vs. stress. Never posted on rogerblench.info (the Internet Archive's index 2015-2025) and the domain is now lost; would have to be requested from Blench/KWEF.

sources.note: The only published comparative phonological analyses of the North Jos (East Kainji) group with tone-marked data for Buji/Jere/Gusu/Sanga/Ribina; Panawa itself was not sampled (then treated as a dialect of Gusu/Sanga), so at best a cluster-level proxy.
